questions.stem: Which item is not a parameter or spatial characteristic of a continuous sinusoidal carrier wave?
questions.hint: Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.
sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 47

answer.explanation: A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Given propagation speed, wavelength follows from frequency and describes its spatial repetition. A discrete pulse is a different waveform description, not a parameter of a continuous sine wave. This distinction concerns the specified carrier model; it does not claim that all pulse modulation is digital, since pulse amplitude and width can vary to carry analog information.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Amplitude specifies the sinusoid’s magnitude.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Wavelength specifies the spatial repetition of the propagating sinusoid.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Phase specifies displacement within the sinusoid’s cycle.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A discrete pulse is a waveform description rather than a sinusoidal parameter.

evidence.quote: Analog signals vary continuously; digital signals use discrete symbol states. Data and signal types are separate: digital bits can modulate an analog carrier. A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.

Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.

sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 49

answer.text: Forwarding local broadcasts is not a normal router function
answer.explanation: Routers forward IP packets between networks and separate broadcast domains. Accordingly internetwork communication and packet forwarding/switching describe routing, whereas ordinary local link broadcasts are not propagated across routers. Packet filtering can accompany the traffic-control function, so A is the normal-function exception, not a claim that no specially configured broadcast relay can exist.

choices.explanation: Traffic filtering can be implemented alongside routing; it is consistent with router security-policy controls.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A router forwards individual packets to next hops, a network-layer packet-switching function.

evidence.quote: Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. questions.stem: Which OSI layer uses acknowledgments, sequencing and receiver flow control for end-to-end process delivery, as illustrated by TCP?
questions.hint: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.
sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 50

answer.explanation: Scope separates otherwise similar mechanisms. Reliable link procedures can acknowledge frames and control a single hop, whereas TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgments and windows between transport endpoints. The explicit end-to-end process-delivery requirement identifies layer 4. IP at layer 3 offers best-effort delivery, and application services build on the transport service rather than defining this TCP reliability machinery.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Layer 2 can provide similar mechanisms only for hop-local link delivery, outside the requested scope.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Layer 4 transport provides TCP’s end-to-end sequencing, acknowledgments and receiver flow control.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: IP best-effort delivery does not provide the indicated ordered acknowledgment/retransmission service.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Application services can build reliability, but the standard link/transport mechanisms named here are not layer-7 duties.

evidence.quote: Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

questions.stem: What is the technique of combining multiple input signals or streams onto a shared transmission link?
questions.hint: Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.
sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 51

answer.explanation: Multiplexing combines input signals or streams so they share a link, using distinctions such as frequency, wavelength or time slots. Demultiplexing is the corresponding receiver operation that separates them. Broadcast and multicast instead describe recipient sets for a message. Link sharing and destination distribution therefore answer different questions, even though a network can use both mechanisms.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Broadcast distributes a message to all members of a broadcast domain rather than combining input streams.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Multicast distributes to a receiver group rather than combining inputs onto a link.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Multiplexing combines inputs onto the shared link.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Demultiplexing separates received multiplexed inputs; it is the reverse operation.

evidence.quote: Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. FDM assigns distinct frequency bands with suitable guard spacing; WDM assigns different optical wavelengths. TDM allocates time slots: synchronous TDM reserves recurrent slots even if an input is idle, while statistical TDM allocates according to demand and needs identification.

Flooding sends copies on eligible outgoing links with duplicate/lifetime controls; random walk picks a neighbor probabilistically. Unicast targets one destination, broadcast all in a scope, multicast a subscribed group and anycast one member sharing an address, normally nearest under routing metrics. Multi-destination packets can list multiple targets; this is not necessarily identical to broadcast. Group multicast trees use mechanisms such as reverse-path checks; Ethernet spanning tree is a different layer-2 mechanism.

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module

Data Link Layer
 The Data Link layer adds reliability to the physical
layer by providing error detection and correction
mechanisms.
 Framing: the Data Link layer receives the data
from Network Layer and divides the stream of bits
into fixed size manageable units called as Frames
and sends it to the physical layer. On the receiver
side, the data link layer receives the stream of bits
from the physical layer and regroups them into
frames and sends them to the Network layer.
 Physical Addressing: The Data link layer appends
the physical address in the header of the frame
before sending it to physical layer.
 Flow control: The data link layer makes sure that
the sender sends the data at a speed at which the
receiver canreceive it else if there is an overflow at
the receiver sidethe data will be lost.
 Error Control: The data link layer imposes error
control mechanism to identify lost or damaged
frames, duplicateframes and then retransmit them.
 Access Control: The data link layer imposes
access control mechanism to determine which
device has right to send data in an multipoint
connection setting.
 Main Responsibility: The main responsibility of
the data link layer is hop to hop transmission of
frames.

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
 At the sending side, the transport layer receives data
from the session layer, divides it into units called
segments and sends it to the network layer.
 To ensure process to process delivery the transport
layer makes use of port address to identify the data
from the sending and receiving process.
 The data can be transported in a connection oriented
or connectionless manner.
 The Transport layer is responsible for segmentation
and reassembly of the message into segments which
bear sequence numbers.

error control functions; but unlike data link layer

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module

Network Layer

deliveredto the receiver despite multiple
intermediate devices.

data from the transport layer, divides it into
packets, addsaddressing information in the
header and passes it tothe data link layer.
 The network layer is responsible for
source todestination of delivery of data.
 The network layer uses logical address
commonlyknown as IP address to recognize
devices on the network.
 Each packet is independent of the other and may
travelusing different routes to reach the receiver
hence may arrive out of turn at the receiver
(Routing).
 The Network layer does not perform any flow
controlor error control
 The main responsibility of Network Layer is
transmission of packets from source to destination

questions.stem: Which one of the following is disadvantage of circuit switching?
questions.hint: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 92

answer.text: Limited scalability due to reserved resources
answer.explanation: Circuit switching reserves resources for an established path. NET31 explains that this offers predictable bandwidth but introduces setup, blocking and unused reservation during silence. Those costs constrain how many simultaneous circuits can be supported as demand grows, making limited scalability the disadvantage among the offered choices.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Predictable performance is a benefit of allocated circuit resources, not the disadvantage requested.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Low transfer latency after setup can be beneficial; the relevant costs include setup and resource reservation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Guaranteed allocated bandwidth is an advantage, although reserving it consumes capacity during silence.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Finite reserved resources and blocking constrain simultaneous connections and therefore scalability as demand grows.

evidence.quote: Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

module_refs.quote:
Circuit Switching: In circuit switching, two

connection before any transfer of data.
 Data transfer: Transfer data is from the source to the
destination. The data may be analog or digital,
depending on the nature of the network. The
connection is generally full-duplex.
 Circuit disconnect: Terminate connection at the end
of data transfer. Signals must be propagated to
deallocate the dedicated resources.

 Store-and-forward

answer.explanation: Interpret interconnected as every node directly connected to every other node: this is the module full-mesh definition. Without directly, all connected topologies would qualify. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Star nodes connect through a central device (PDF 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Ring nodes directly connect only to two neighbors (PDF 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Full mesh explicitly connects every node to every other (PDF 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Tree is listed but not defined as all-pairs direct connectivity (PDF 23, 23, 23.)

evidence.quote: Physical topology describes link layout; logical topology describes communication/access relationships. Point-to-point links join two endpoints; multipoint links share a medium. A full mesh consists of point-to-point links.

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.

module_refs.quote:
Mesh Topology: in this topology devices are
connected with many redundant interconnections
between network nodes. In a full mesh topology,
every node has a connection to every other node in
the network, which makes it the most expensive
topology over all the other topologies. The number of
cables grows fast as the number of nodes increases,
and it can be calculated by using the general formula
((n (n – 1)) /2), where n is the number of nodes in the

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Star Topology: in this topology, each node is
connected directly to a central device called a hub or
a switch. Data on a star network passes through the
central device (switch) before continuing to its
destination. The central device manages and controls
all functions of the network. This configuration is
common with twisted pair cable. RJ-45 Connectors
are used to connect the cable to the Network Interface
Card (NIC) of each computer. Its advantages include,
ease of installation and reconfiguration, robust (ease
of fault identification and isolation), link failure only
affects device(s) connected to that link, and is less
expensive than mesh. Its drawbacks include more
cable requirements (than bus and ring) and single
point of failure (if central device fail, the whole
system will be down).

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Ring Topology: in this topology, all devices are
connected to one another in the shape of a closed
loop, so that each device is connected directly to two
other devices, one on either side of it. Some of its
advantages include, easy to install and reconfigure,
less expensive (than mesh), and performance is even
despite the number of users. Its cons include, break in
the ring (such as a disabled station) can disable the
entire network, and limitations on media and traffic
(limitation on ring length and number of devices).

answer.text: IPv6 is logical address; IPv4 is 32-bit and IPv6 is 128-bit
answer.explanation: IPv4 addresses contain 32 bits, and IPv6 addresses contain 128 bits. Both are logical network-layer addresses, so IPv6 being logical is compatible with the width comparison. Physical or MAC addressing belongs to the link layer. The corrected selection instruction allows both true statements to be selected while retaining the original factual comparisons and the two incorrect distractors.

evidence.quote: IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.

IPv6 has 128-bit hexadecimal addresses, flexible prefixes and no IPv4-style broadcast. Sources, not routers, fragment IPv6 packets. IPv6 does not automatically encrypt traffic or make authentication unnecessary. Compare IPv6’s larger 128-bit address space and encryption support separately; specify the property being evaluated.

Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 153

answer.text: Neither induced nor crosstalk names a transmission medium
answer.explanation: The note identifies cables and unguided radio/microwave/infrared as transmission media. Crosstalk instead names interference from nearby channels in NET06, and induced alone does not name a medium in the note. Regardless of the vague direct-transmission phrase, none of A–C supplies a listed medium, so D is the supported exclusion response.

evidence.quote: Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.

Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.

answer.explanation: Transport supplies process-to-process delivery and segmentation. The network layer handles logical addressing and routing, the data-link layer handles hop delivery of frames, and the physical layer transports bits or symbols. Restoring the four readable source rows gives the transport option its proper position. Reliability remains protocol-dependent: identifying transport does not imply that every transport protocol guarantees delivery.

A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

answer.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, commonly written as four decimal octets, and its subnet mask selects a prefix within those 32 bits. IPv6 addresses instead contain 128 bits. evidence.quote: Write IPv4 as four decimal octets 0–255, or as 32 binary bits. Use weights 128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1 within each octet. Thus 11000001 10000011 00011011 11111111 is 193.131.27.255. questions.stem:
What is the main goal of data compression while it paths in different
network layers? Its goal is to:

options.label: C
options.text: Select the best path of destination devices

questions.hint: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.
sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 16

answer.explanation: NET19 distinguishes reducing representation size from hiding content. Compression targets the amount of data needed to represent information, while encryption provides concealment and routing selects paths. Therefore minimizing size is the compression goal; combining it with security and path selection in the all option misattributes unrelated functions.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Securing or concealing content is an encryption/security function, not the primary goal of compression.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Compression reduces representation size, directly matching minimization of data size.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Path selection belongs to routing rather than the representation-size transformation performed by compression.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Only size reduction describes compression here; security and route selection are separate functions.

evidence.quote: OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.

Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.

answer.explanation: POP3 retrieves stored messages, while IMAP accesses and synchronizes mailboxes held on the server. SMTP instead submits and relays messages between mail-system components. evidence.quote: HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. questions.stem:
Which internet layer address is responsible for providing diagnostic
functions and reporting errors or conditions regarding the delivery of IP
packets?
questions.hint: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.
sources: Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 97

answer.explanation: ICMP reports transit problems and supports destination-unreachable, echo and timeout diagnostics. The stem calls it an address, but asks for a protocol by its functions. Evidence: PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: IP supplies best-effort datagram delivery (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: ARP resolves IP to hardware address (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: ICMP explicitly provides error/diagnostic messages (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

choices.label: D

evidence.quote: ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. It bridges the network/link addressing boundary and is often classified at the link layer; calling ARP simply a network protocol uses a loose textbook convention. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP/DHCP support boot configuration. ICMP reports errors and diagnostics; IGMP manages IPv4 multicast membership. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.

IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.

works at the Network layer and is used by IP for
many different services. ICMP is a management
protocol and messagingservice provider for IP. The
following are some common events and messages
that ICMP relates to:
Destination Unreachable: If a router can‘t send an
IP datagram any further, it uses ICMP to send a
message back to the sender, advising it of the
situation.
Buffer Full: If a router‘s memory buffer for
receiving incoming datagrams is full, it will use
ICMP to send out this message until the congestion
abates.
Hops: Each IP datagram is allotted a certain number
of routers, called hops, to pass through. If it reaches
its limitof hops before arriving at its destination, the
last router to receive that datagram deletes it. The
executioner router then uses ICMP to send an
obituary message, informing the sending machine of
the demise of its datagram.
Ping (Packet Internet Groper) uses ICMP echo
messages to check the physical and logical
connectivity of machineson a network.
Traceroute Using ICMP timeouts, Traceroute is
used to discover the path a packet takes as it
traverses an Internetwork.

Address orcommonly known as IP address that is used

used bya device on the network to find its Internet
address when it knows its physical address.

Network Layer or IP
Also called as the Internetwork Layer (IP). It holds the
IP protocol which is a network layer protocol and is
responsiblefor source to destination transmission of
data.
The Internetworking Protocol (IP) is a connection-less &
unreliable protocol.
It is a best effort delivery service. i.e. there is no error
checking in IP, it simply sends the data and relies on its
underlying layers to get the data transmitted to the
destination.Even if it is unreliable IP cannot be
considered weak and useless; since it provides only the
functionality that is requiredfor transmitting data thereby
giving maximum efficiency.
Since there is no mechanism of error detection or
correction in IP, there will be no delay introduced on a
medium where thereis no error at all.

evidence.quote: A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

Each switch port separates collision domains; full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has no collisions and does not use CSMA/CD. Switching permits independent conversations simultaneously. Broadcasts still reach the VLAN unless another control filters them. A layer-3 switch also routes, so device marketing names do not override the function being examined.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

questions.stem: Compare circuit switching versus datagram packet switching. An advantage of circuit switching is it:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Can guarantee the performance delivered to end hosts.

options.label: C
options.text: Establishes a connection before sending data.

options.text: Is efficient when the amount of traffic to be sent by end hosts varies over time.

questions.hint: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.
sources: Mock exam 1 · Question 12

answer.explanation: The reserved-resource circuit supports predictable allocated bandwidth and performance, the advantage contrasted with datagram links shared statistically. Establishing a connection is a procedural characteristic and imposes setup cost rather than itself guaranteeing a benefit. The note explicitly identifies blocking and wasted reservation during silence, ruling out the nonblocking and variable-traffic-efficiency claims.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Different endpoint line rates are not the reserved-circuit advantage established in the note.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Reserved resources provide predictable allocated bandwidth and can guarantee the agreed performance to endpoints.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Setup is a characteristic of circuit operation, but is not itself the performance advantage requested.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Circuit switching establishes reserved resources; packet-versus-signal wording does not describe its advantage.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: NET31 explicitly identifies blocking as a circuit-switching tradeoff.

choices.label: F
choices.explanation: Reservations can be wasted during silence, making highly variable traffic less efficient on fixed circuits.

evidence.quote: Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.

evidence.quote: A computer network connects computers or other devices so they can exchange information and share resources such as files, storage and printers. The interconnection uses both hardware and software; neither hardware alone nor software alone is the definition of the whole network.

An intranet serves an organization internally; an extranet exposes selected services to approved outsiders. Neither term alone specifies geographic size. A client requests a service; a server supplies it. Peer systems may perform both roles. Dedicated servers concentrate on service workloads but can still be clients of DNS, backup or update services. A ten-user cutoff is a teaching guideline, not a technical law. Centralization simplifies administration but creates dependencies; peer networks still need security.

evidence.quote: PAN connects personal devices, such as Bluetooth accessories. LAN covers a local building or campus; MAN spans a metropolitan region; WAN connects distant regions. Device count alone does not determine the category. The Internet is a global network of networks, commonly the largest example of a WAN.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.

questions.stem: A __________ is a device that forwards packets between networks by processing the routing information included in the packet.
questions.hint: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.
sources: Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 11

answer.explanation: Router forwarding explicitly compares the destination IP to routing table entries to choose the next path between networks. Evidence: PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Bridge filters same-protocol LAN traffic using MAC (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A firewall permits/denies access; that is not the defining routing-table function (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Router matches the stated destination-IP routing procedure (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Hub repeats/broadcasts without destination-route analysis (PDF 12, 12, 12, 48.)

evidence.quote: Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

answer.explanation: Physical-layer standardized interfaces deliver bit-by-bit or symbol-by-symbol; processes and ports are transport concerns. Evidence: PDF 14, 16.

evidence.quote: Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.

answer.explanation: Optical fiber guides light, resists electromagnetic interference and supports high-capacity, long-reach links with suitable optics and installation. answer.explanation: Digital modulation explicitly converts digital data to analog signals; ASK/FSK/PSK are its given methods. The other names are listed as analog modulation of analog data. Evidence: PDF 13.

evidence.quote: ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.

A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.

evidence.quote: Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. evidence.quote: CRC expands to Cyclic Redundancy Check.

Detection adds redundancy but does not guarantee correction. Even parity adds a bit so the total number of ones is even: 1011 needs parity 1. It detects every odd number of bit flips but misses even counts. CRC treats bits as a polynomial and appends the XOR-division remainder; the receiver repeats the division. Internet checksums add words with end-around carry and complement the sum. A burst spans from the first corrupted bit through the last, including unchanged interior bits. Retransmission or sufficient forward-error-correcting redundancy is needed for recovery.

questions.stem: For IPv4 as described in the note, which listed function is not provided by IP itself? Here “error control” means header checksum error detection.
questions.hint: Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.
sources: Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 29

answer.explanation: IPv4 supports logical packet delivery across networks, including routing, and checks its header with a checksum. The use of error control therefore refers to detection, not reliable end-to-end recovery. TCP supplies congestion control to protect network capacity; IPv4 itself does not provide TCP’s congestion-control service. The question separates those protocol services instead of denying that the network layer ever detects errors.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Routing is explicitly a network-layer function, so it cannot be the requested exception.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Forwarding packets between networks is an established network-layer responsibility.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Congestion control of the kind protecting network capacity is a TCP service rather than a service supplied by IPv4 itself.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: IPv4 detects header corruption with its checksum, so error detection is present under the stated meaning.

evidence.quote: The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.

evidence.quote: IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Link-layer LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control; MAC handles medium-dependent addressing/access and frame delivery. Network addressing belongs to layer 3. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. questions.stem: At a sending host, transport identifies data from different application endpoints using ports and forms segments or datagrams. To which OSI layer does it pass these units directly?

answer.explanation: On the sending path, transport creates segments or datagrams and hands them to the network layer for packet delivery. The network layer then uses the data-link layer, which in turn uses physical signaling. Ports distinguish application endpoints; this multiplexing does not merge unrelated applications into one undifferentiated TCP byte stream. The answer follows the immediate downward interface in the OSI stack.

choices.explanation: Data link is below network, not immediately below transport.

choices.label: D

evidence.quote: Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

TCP setup creates a logical transport connection, not a reserved physical circuit. Ports allow multiplexing separate applications over IP; they do not combine all applications into one TCP byte stream. TCP – Transmission Control Protocol: TCP is a reliable
connection-oriented, reliable protocol. i.e. a connection is
established between the sender and receiver before the data can
be transmitted. It divides the data it receives from the upper
layer into segments and tags a sequence number to each
segment which is used at the receiving end for reordering of
data.
UDP – User Datagram Protocol: UDP is a simple protocol
used for process to process transmission. It is an unreliable,
connectionless protocol for applications that do not require flow
control or error control. It simply adds port address, checksum
and length information to the data it receives from the upper
layer.

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
TCP and UDP must use port numbers to communicate
with the upper layers, because they‘re what keep track of
different conversations crossing the network
simultaneously. These port numbers identify the source
and destination application or process in the TCP
segment. There are 216 = 65,536 ports available.
Well-known ports: The port numbers range from 0 to
1,023.
Registered ports: The port numbers range from 1,024 to
49,151. Registered ports are used by applications or
services that need to have consistent port assignments.
Dynamic or private ports: The port numbers range from
49,152 to 65,535.

questions.stem: Using “end-to-end” for application service and “process-to-process” for the transport service beneath it, which service does the application layer offer?

options.label: C
options.text: Both End to end and Process to process

questions.hint: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.
sources: Data Communication & Networking practice questions · Question 47

answer.explanation: The question explicitly separates an application service from the underlying transport service. The note describes end-to-end application service as building on process-to-process transport. Under those named scopes, the application layer offers the end-to-end service, while process delivery identifies the transport boundary. Combining both would collapse the distinction being tested; none of the mentioned fails because the application-service term is present.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: End-to-end is the stated application-service scope.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Process-to-process names the underlying transport service in this question.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The combination assigns the underlying transport-service term to the application layer, contrary to the stated distinction.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The stated application-service term is offered in A.

evidence.quote: The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. Distinguish end-to-end application service from its underlying process-to-process transport.

Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.

questions.stem: In TCP connection establishment procedure, if a client chooses Initial Sequence Number of 395, and server chooses 260, then:

options.label: A
options.text: The 1st segment sent will contain sequence number of 396

options.label: B
options.text: The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 261

options.label: C
options.text: The 3rd segment sent will contain sequence number of 261

options.label: D
options.text: The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396

options.label: E
options.text: The 2nd segment sent will contain sequence number of 395

options.label: F
options.text: The 3rd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396

questions.hint: Trace the handshake in order, keeping each endpoint’s sequence and acknowledgment fields separate.
sources: Mock exam 3 · Question 4

answer.explanation: SYN consumes one sequence position. The first segment is client SYN seq395. The server’s second segment is SYN+ACK seq260 ack396, acknowledging the client SYN. The third is client ACK seq396 ack261. Comparing those fields shows only D matches; sequence numbers and acknowledgment numbers must not be swapped between endpoints.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The first client SYN uses its initial sequence number 395, not the next position 396.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The second segment acknowledges the client SYN with 396; 261 is the later acknowledgment of the server SYN.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The third segment’s sequence number is the client’s next position 396, not the server acknowledgment value 261.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The server’s SYN+ACK acknowledges client ISN 395 plus one, giving 396.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: The second segment is sent by the server with its own sequence number 260.

choices.label: F
choices.explanation: The third segment acknowledges server ISN 260 plus one, giving 261 rather than 396.

evidence.quote: TCP establishes state with SYN, SYN+ACK, then ACK. SYN consumes one sequence position even with no application bytes. An acknowledgment states the next expected sequence number. For client ISN=395 and server ISN=260: client sends SYN seq395; server sends SYN+ACK seq260 ack396; client sends ACK seq396 ack261. Later byte counts advance sequence numbers. FIN also consumes one sequence position.

questions.stem: For IPv4 when fragmentation is permitted, which option gives the complete set of nodes that may fragment packets and the location of reassembly?

options.label: A
options.text: Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the destination host

options.label: B
options.text: Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host

options.label: C
options.text: Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the routers and destination host

options.label: D
options.text: Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the routers and destination host

options.label: E
options.text: IP does not support Fragmentation and Re-assembly.

questions.hint: Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.
sources: Mock exam 3 · Question 5

answer.text: Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host
answer.explanation: IPv4 permits both the source and a router to fragment packets when fragmentation is allowed and an outgoing MTU requires it. The destination reassembles the fragments. Source-only fragmentation omits a permitted IPv4 case; it instead resembles the IPv6 restriction. Adding intermediate-router reassembly is incorrect. Naming IPv4 and asking for the complete permitted set makes the version-specific distinction explicit.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A source may fragment, but this option omits permitted IPv4 router fragmentation.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: IPv4 sources and routers may fragment; only the destination reassembles.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Neither cited IP fragmentation rule places reassembly at intermediate routers.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Destination reassembly is required; the additional router reassembly claim is unsupported for either version.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: Both version-specific rules support fragmentation and reassembly, although the allowed fragmenting nodes differ.

evidence.quote: The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.

IPv6 has 128-bit hexadecimal addresses, flexible prefixes and no IPv4-style broadcast. Sources, not routers, fragment IPv6 packets. IPv6 does not automatically encrypt traffic or make authentication unnecessary. Compare IPv6’s larger 128-bit address space and encryption support separately; specify the property being evaluated.

questions.stem: Packets in one TCP connection can be distinguished from packets in another TCP connection by:

options.label: A
options.text: Source port, destination port, protocol number

options.label: B
options.text: Source IP address, destination IP address, protocol number

options.label: C
options.text: Source port, destination port, source IP address, destination IP address

options.label: D
options.text: Source IP address, destination IP address

questions.hint: Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration.
sources: Mock exam 3 · Question 6

answer.text: Both IP addresses and both port numbers
answer.explanation: All packets under discussion are already TCP, so their protocol identity is common. Distinguishing arbitrary simultaneous connections needs the endpoint four-tuple: source IP, destination IP, source port and destination port. Addresses alone cannot distinguish separate applications between the same hosts; ports alone can repeat between different hosts. C supplies all four required fields.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Ports and protocol can repeat between different host pairs, so this omits necessary IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Two hosts can have several simultaneous TCP connections; addresses and TCP protocol alone do not distinguish them.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The source/destination IP addresses and source/destination ports form the TCP connection four-tuple.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An IP-address pair cannot distinguish multiple connections between the same two hosts.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: The same source/destination port pair can be used with different IP-address endpoints.

choices.label: F
choices.explanation: Every connection in the stem uses TCP, so protocol number alone distinguishes none of them.

questions.stem: Compared to other common topologies in LANs (such as bus, mesh, ring), which of the following is a disadvantage of using a star topology for LAN?

options.label: A
options.text: Poor performance due to sharing of point-to-multipoint links between users

options.label: B
options.text: Failure of a single station results in no stations being able to communicate

options.label: C
options.text: Failure of a single link results in no stations being able to communicate

options.label: D
options.text: Each station requires many network interfaces

options.label: E
options.text: Too many links needed in the network

options.label: F
options.text: Failure of a special node results in no stations being able to communicate

questions.hint: Draw the links and identify shared components, alternate paths and the effect of the specified failure or growth requirement.
sources: Mock exam 2 · Question 19

answer.text: Failure of a special node results in no stations being able to communicate
answer.explanation: The star description explicitly calls its hub/switch a single point of failure: failure of that central device brings the whole system down. Ordinary station/link failure is isolated. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Star has separate central links, not the bus shared-backbone defect (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Failure of an ordinary station does not remove the central device (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The module says a link failure affects only its attached device (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Many interfaces per station is the full-mesh burden (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: Star uses more cable than bus/ring but less than mesh, so this is not the distinctive universal comparison (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

choices.label: F
choices.explanation: The special central node is explicitly a single point of failure (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

evidence.quote: Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.
A full undirected mesh of n nodes needs n(n-1)/2 links and n-1 interfaces per node. For 50 nodes: 50×49/2=1225 links. Redundant paths improve fault tolerance at greater cable and interface cost.

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Star Topology: in this topology, each node is
connected directly to a central device called a hub or
a switch. Data on a star network passes through the
central device (switch) before continuing to its
destination. The central device manages and controls
all functions of the network. This configuration is
common with twisted pair cable. RJ-45 Connectors
are used to connect the cable to the Network Interface
Card (NIC) of each computer. Its advantages include,
ease of installation and reconfiguration, robust (ease
of fault identification and isolation), link failure only
affects device(s) connected to that link, and is less
expensive than mesh. Its drawbacks include more
cable requirements (than bus and ring) and single
point of failure (if central device fail, the whole
system will be down).

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Mesh Topology: in this topology devices are
connected with many redundant interconnections
between network nodes. In a full mesh topology,
every node has a connection to every other node in
the network, which makes it the most expensive
topology over all the other topologies. The number of
cables grows fast as the number of nodes increases,
and it can be calculated by using the general formula
((n (n – 1)) /2), where n is the number of nodes in the

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Bus Topology: in this topology all devices are
connected to a central cable, called the bus or
backbone, which is terminated at its ends. The
purpose of the terminators is to stop the signal from
bouncing, thereby clearing the cable so that other
computers can send data. Message transmitted along
the Bus is visible to all computers connected to the
backbone cable. As the message arrives at each
workstation, the workstation checks the destination
address contained in the message either to process or
drop the packet if it matches or not respectively. Its
advantages are, ease of installation and less amount
of cable requirement. Its main drawback is, the entire
network will be shut down if there is a break in the
main cable.

module_refs.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking module
module_refs.quote:
Ring Topology: in this topology, all devices are
connected to one another in the shape of a closed
loop, so that each device is connected directly to two
other devices, one on either side of it. Some of its
advantages include, easy to install and reconfigure,
less expensive (than mesh), and performance is even
despite the number of users. Its cons include, break in
the ring (such as a disabled station) can disable the
entire network, and limitations on media and traffic
(limitation on ring length and number of devices).

questions.stem: For IPv4 networks, distinguish interface IP addresses, transport port numbers and the IPv4 Protocol header field. Which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The protocol number commonly used by web server applications is 80

options.label: B
options.text: Every application must use a well-known port number

options.label: C
options.text: Each host and router in the Internet has only a single IP address

options.label: D
options.text: Client applications may dynamically select port numbers

options.label: E
options.text: A protocol number is used to indicate the version of IP being used

questions.hint: Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration.
sources: Mock exam 2 · Question 20

answer.text: Client applications may dynamically select port numbers
answer.explanation: Client applications commonly use dynamically selected ephemeral ports. Ports identify transport endpoints, whereas the IPv4 Protocol field identifies the carried upper-layer protocol, such as TCP or UDP. The separate Version field identifies the IP version. Port 80 is a usual HTTP service port, not an IP protocol number. Hosts and routers can have multiple addressed interfaces, so they are not restricted to one IP address.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: 80 is a usual HTTP port number, not the IPv4 Protocol value for HTTP.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Clients may use ephemeral ports, so a well-known port is not mandatory for every application.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A device can have multiple addressed interfaces and therefore multiple IP addresses.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Clients may dynamically select ephemeral transport ports.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: The IPv4 Protocol field identifies the upper-layer protocol; the Version field identifies the IP version.

evidence.quote: An IP address identifies a network interface rather than limiting a whole computer to one address. A computer or router can have several interfaces and addresses. Under a supplied IPv4 prefix, leading bits identify the network and the remaining bits identify an address within that network; a MAC address is a separate link-layer identifier.

TCP and UDP port fields are 16 bits, allowing numbers from 0 through 65535. Well-known ports are 0–1023, registered ports are 1024–49151, and dynamic/private ports are 49152–65535. Client endpoints can use dynamically selected ports instead of every application requiring a well-known assignment. These port numbers are distinct from the IP version and upper-protocol fields.

IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.

questions.stem: If you would like to give IP address to 57 hosts from your IP prefix which subnet mask do you use most effectively?
questions.hint: Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule.
sources: Mock exam 2 · Question 21

answer.explanation: For 57 hosts choose the smallest offered block with at least 57 total addresses: /26 (192=11000000) has 64. The next smaller /27 has only 32, and /25 wastes twice the space. Even the conventional two reserved addresses leave /26 sufficient. Evidence: PDF 19, 19.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: 248 gives only eight total addresses (PDF 19, 19.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: 240 gives only 16 (PDF 19, 19.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: 224 gives only 32 (PDF 19, 19.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: 128 gives 128 and uses more space than necessary (PDF 19, 19.)

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: 192 gives 64, the smallest offered sufficient block (PDF 19, 19.)

evidence.quote: For H hosts, choose the smallest h satisfying 2^h-2≥H, then p=32-h. For 24 hosts use /27; 52 or 57 use /26; 100 use /25; 500 use /23. For at least six equal subnets choose b=3. A Class C /24 split to /27 yields eight subnets. Always check both the number of subnets and the host capacity.

A /p IPv4 prefix has p leading one bits followed by 32-p zeros. Partial octet masks are 128,192,224,240,248,252,254. /19 is 255.255.224.0; /20 is 255.255.240.0; /21 is 255.255.248.0, correcting the study guide’s 255.248.0.0 mistake.

evidence.quote: A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

answer.text: In packet switching, an end-to-end connection has to be established
answer.explanation: Datagram switching divides messages into packets and forwards those packets independently without requiring end-to-end connection establishment. Circuit switching reserves resources along a path. Statistical sharing lets bursty packet traffic use capacity that would otherwise remain reserved but idle; this is a conditional utilization advantage, not a universal claim that packets outperform circuits for every workload or metric.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Packet switching divides messages into smaller packets.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Connectionless datagrams do not require end-to-end connection setup.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Circuit switching reserves channel resources for the connection.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: For bursty traffic, shared packet links can avoid idle dedicated reservations; the qualified statement is true.

evidence.quote: Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.

 Store-and-forward

evidence.quote: Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.

Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

answer.text: Travel distance is not an explicit channel-capacity formula variable
answer.explanation: NET05 gives Nyquist in terms of bandwidth and signal states, and Shannon in terms of bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio. Distance is not an independent variable in those simplified capacity formulas, so A is the intended comparison. It can still affect practical achievable rate through attenuation and delay. The image confirms travel distance despite noise in another extracted option.

evidence.quote: TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

OSI session roles establish/manage dialogs and can coordinate checkpoints so transfer resumes after interruption. Presentation roles translate encodings and handle compression/encryption. Compression reduces representation size; encryption hides content and need not shrink it. Application protocols provide services directly to applications. Practical implementations distribute these functions differently; TLS is not proof of a separate physical presentation-layer device.

evidence.quote: Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.

For legacy fixed Ethernet port roles, PCs and router Ethernet endpoints use the same endpoint role, while ordinary switch ports use the opposite role. Thus a direct router-to-PC link uses crossover wiring; PC-to-switch or router-to-switch uses straight-through wiring. Automatic MDI-X can remove the need to choose the crossover manually.

questions.stem:
Given a situation two hosts attempt on a half-duplex Ethernet LAN to send data concurrently, resulting in a collision and subsequent to this collision,
what will the hosts do?

options.label: A
options.text: An electrical pulse indicates that the collision has cleared

options.label: B
options.text: The router on the segment will signal that the collision has cleared

options.label: C
options.text: The jam signal indicates that the collision has been cleared

options.label: D
options.text: The hosts will attempt to resume transmission after a time delay has expired

questions.hint: Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions.
sources: Computer Science model exam collection · Question 33

answer.text: Stop and retry after random backoff
answer.explanation: NET14 gives the collision sequence: detect, jam, stop and retry after random backoff. The jam indicates the collision itself, not that it has cleared. There is no router-coordinated clearance procedure or electrical clearance pulse in the stated rule. Therefore waiting for a delay and attempting transmission again is the supported host behavior.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The defined procedure uses collision indication and backoff; it does not include a collision-cleared electrical pulse.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Ethernet collision recovery is performed by the hosts’ MAC procedure, not a router clearance signal.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A jam announces the collision; it does not certify that the shared medium is clear.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: After stopping, hosts retry following random backoff, matching a delay before another transmission attempt.

evidence.quote: Random access allows contention: ALOHA sends opportunistically; CSMA senses before sending. In legacy half-duplex Ethernet, CSMA/CD detects collision, sends a jam indication, stops, and retries after random backoff. The jam signals a collision, not its clearance. Wi-Fi 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with waiting/backoff and acknowledgments; sensing does not eliminate hidden-terminal collisions.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the use of switches and hubs for network connectivity in the network?

options.label: B

questions.hint: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions.
sources: Computer Science model exam collection · Question 41

answer.explanation: NET10 says each switch port separates collision domains, whereas a half-duplex hub repeats traffic into one shared collision domain. Switches still flood broadcasts within their VLAN, and hubs do not inspect and filter destination frames. The note gives no universal switch-versus-hub processing-time advantage, so A is the supported claim.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Replacing a shared hub segment with separate switch ports divides the network into additional collision domains.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The note establishes no universal lower switch processing time; a hub simply repeats signals.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Switches flood broadcasts within the VLAN unless another control filters them.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Hubs repeat physical signals and neither learn MAC destinations nor filter frames.

evidence.quote: Each switch port separates collision domains; full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has no collisions and does not use CSMA/CD. Switching permits independent conversations simultaneously. Broadcasts still reach the VLAN unless another control filters them. A layer-3 switch also routes, so device marketing names do not override the function being examined.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

evidence.quote: The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. Distinguish end-to-end application service from its underlying process-to-process transport.

Routing computes paths; forwarding chooses a next hop for an individual packet. Select the matching route with the longest prefix, then apply the routing system’s tie-breaking criteria. A default /0 matches when nothing more specific does. Static routes are configured; dynamic protocols exchange reachability. Distance vector uses neighbor estimates, while link state distributes link information and computes shortest paths. Interior protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP exchanges routes between systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a primary function of the network layer in the OSI model?
questions.hint: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 474

answer.text: Flow control is not a primary network-layer duty
answer.explanation: The network layer supplies logical addressing/routing and, for IPv4, fragmentation when permitted. Flow control instead protects a receiver in transport or hop-local link procedures, as NET14 and NET17 explain. Thus C is not a primary network-layer function in this layer model, without claiming that all control mechanisms belong exclusively to one layer.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Routing is explicitly a main network-layer duty in the NET12 layer table.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Logical addressing is explicitly assigned to the network layer.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Receiver flow control is described at link and transport scope rather than as a primary network duty.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: NET16 supports IPv4 fragmentation by sources and routers, a network-protocol function.

evidence.quote: The IPv4 checksum protects its header; IP does not lack error checking altogether. Identification, flags and offset support fragmentation. IPv4 sources and routers may fragment when allowed; reassembly occurs at the destination. If DF is set and the next MTU is too small, forwarding fails and an ICMP diagnostic may be returned.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.
